gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 10W laser module for the $269 Falcon A1C costs $139 more on Creality's US store, so a 10W A1C comes to about $408 for a 150 × 150 mm bed, while the 10W Falcon A1 is $549 there for 381 × 305 mm (about 5.2 times the area), and the xTool M2 is $499.
standout_why: Compared against maker-wise (cited), planet3dp, engraverpicker, the xTool beginner guide (cited) and Tom's Hardware's best-picks page (cited). The last two cut off after the headline when fetched, so their content could not be checked. planet3dp already gives the A1C's 150 × 150 mm bed and a $269 price with the 5W module. engraverpicker gives a 10W A1C at $369. maker-wise already has the A1 Pro at $1,099. None of them gives the $139 A1C 10W module price or works out what a 10W A1C costs against the A1 or M2. ChatGPT's own answer gave the A1 Pro at $879.99 and the A1 at $466.99, both from Micro Center. Creality's US store charges $1,099 and $549 today. I could not open Micro Center to check its prices.
decides: This confirms the xTool M2 10W as the default beginner pick at $499 on the maker's store. At maker prices the Falcon A1 is $50 more, so it only wins as 'best value' at the Micro Center price ChatGPT quoted, which I could not check. It also weakens the A1C as the budget pick: a shopper who wants 10W pays about $408 and still gets about a fifth of the A1's bed area. The A1 Pro's maker price ($1,099) is $219 above the price ChatGPT showed, which puts it in the xTool S1's range ($1,299).
